records.name: EU Startup and Scaleup Strategy: Choose Europe to start and scale
records.description: Commission communication adopted on 28 May 2025 that aims to make Europe a great place for starting and growing global technology-driven companies. It sets out actions in five areas: an innovation-friendly regulatory environment, better access to finance, faster market uptake and expansion, access to talent, and access to infrastructure, networks and services. Flagship follow-ups include the 28th regime (EU Inc.), the European Innovation Act, the Scaleup Europe Fund and a European Innovation Investment Pact.
objectives: Reduce fragmentation, administrative burden and regulatory complexity for innovative companies
Build a larger, more integrated EU venture capital market with greater involvement of institutional investors
Speed up the journey from lab to market and cross-border expansion
Improve access to highly skilled talent
Simplify and harmonise access to research and technology infrastructures and services
records.status_note: Non-legislative strategy being rolled out through follow-up acts: the EU Inc. proposal was tabled on 18 March 2026, the Scaleup Europe Fund launched on 3 June 2026, the European Innovation Act was proposed on 9 September 2026 and the institutional investors pact launched on 22 September 2026; an implementation report is due by end-2027.

latest_development.text: The Commission and the EIB Group launched the European Institutional Investors Pact, a voluntary framework under which 13 institutional investors signalled intent to invest in European venture and growth funds; it delivers the strategy's planned investment pact.

records.name: Regulation on the 28th Regime Corporate Legal Framework (EU Inc.)
records.description: Proposed regulation creating an optional, harmonised EU corporate legal form, 'EU Inc.', that would be recognised in every Member State alongside national company forms. The proposal provides for digital-by-default formation and filings, no minimum capital requirement, and an EU employee stock option scheme with harmonised timing of taxation. It is aimed primarily at startups, scaleups and innovative SMEs but is open to any company.
objectives: Offer a single optional company form usable across the Single Market
Enable fully online incorporation (target of 48 hours and costs below €100)
Digitise procedures across the company life cycle with once-only data transmission
Harmonise employee stock option schemes and their tax timing
Provide faster, digital insolvency procedures for EU Inc. companies
records.institution: European Commission; European Parliament (JURI); Council of the EU (Competitiveness)
records.status_note: Commission proposal COM(2026) 321 (procedure 2026/0074(COD)) is pending: the Council adopted its position on 23 October 2026, but Parliament's JURI committee has not yet adopted a report (a vote failed on 19 October 2026); the European Council has called for agreement by end-2026.

records.name: European Innovation Act
records.description: Proposed regulation establishing a framework of measures to strengthen the Union innovation ecosystem (and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/1001), adopted by the Commission on 9 September 2026. It would create a harmonised EU framework for R&D public procurement including joint cross-border procurement, an EU-wide framework for valuing intellectual property to support IP-backed finance, and a digital marketplace for commercialising IP. A separate proposal on regulatory sandboxes was presented alongside it.
objectives: Speed the path of innovations from research to market and cross-border scale-up
Give legal certainty to R&D public procurement and enable joint procurement across Member States
Unlock IP-backed financing through a common IP valuation framework
Create an EU marketplace linking buyers and sellers of IP assets, notably in deep tech
Reduce dependence on non-EU suppliers of innovative products and services
records.status_note: Commission proposal COM(2026) 567 (procedure 2026/0264(COD)) of 9 September 2026 is at the start of the ordinary legislative procedure; no Council or Parliament position yet.

records.name: European Innovation Council
records.description: The European Innovation Council is Horizon Europe's Pillar III flagship for identifying, developing and scaling breakthrough technologies, with a €10.1 billion budget under Horizon Europe. It funds from early research (Pathfinder) through technology transfer (Transition) to startup and SME scale-up (Accelerator, STEP Scale Up), combining grants with direct equity managed by the EIC Fund. The EIC Fund, established in 2020, is its venture capital arm with over €4 billion in capitalisation and 300+ portfolio companies, and is the umbrella for the Scaleup Europe Fund.
objectives: Support breakthrough and deep tech innovation from research to scale-up
Provide patient capital and co-investment to startups and SMEs via the EIC Fund
Close the scale-up financing gap for strategic technologies (STEP Scale Up, Scaleup Europe Fund)
Since June 2026, extend support to defence and dual-use technologies
records.institution: European Commission; European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA); EIC Board; EIC Fund
records.status_note: Fully-fledged EIC launched in March 2021 under Horizon Europe after a 2018-2020 pilot; the 2026 Work Programme (over €1.4bn) was amended in June 2026 to open the Accelerator and STEP Scale Up to dual-use technologies and add a €100m STEP Defence Scale Up call.

records.name: Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform
records.description: Regulation (EU) 2024/795 established STEP to boost investment in critical technologies by steering and reinforcing existing EU programmes (including Horizon Europe/EIC, InvestEU, Innovation Fund, European Defence Fund and cohesion funds) rather than creating a new fund. It covers digital and deep tech, clean and resource-efficient technologies and biotechnologies, and since the 2025 defence mini-omnibus also defence technologies. It introduced the Sovereignty Seal quality label and the STEP Portal listing funding opportunities.
objectives: Support development and manufacturing of critical technologies in the EU and their value chains
Reduce strategic dependencies of the Union
Address labour and skills shortages in STEP sectors
Signal high-quality projects through the Sovereignty Seal to help them access cumulative or alternative funding
records.status_note: In force since 1 March 2024; Regulation (EU) 2025/2653 (defence mini-omnibus) added defence technologies as a fourth STEP sector, reflected in the Commission's second guidance note of 23 December 2025.

records.name: InvestEU Programme
records.description: InvestEU, established by Regulation (EU) 2021/523, uses an EU budget guarantee to back financing by the EIB Group and other implementing partners, with a target of mobilising more than €372 billion of additional investment over 2021-2027. It comprises the InvestEU Fund, the InvestEU Advisory Hub and the InvestEU Portal, covering the green and digital transitions, innovation, SMEs, social investment and skills. The December 2025 'Omnibus II' amendment (Regulation (EU) 2025/2005) raised the EU guarantee and simplified reporting.
objectives: Mobilise public and private investment in EU policy priorities through an EU budget guarantee
Improve access to finance for SMEs, startups and innovative companies
Support green and digital transitions, innovation, social investment and skills
Increase risk-taking capacity for strategic investments, including Clean Industrial Deal priorities
records.institution: European Commission (DG ECFIN); EIB Group and other implementing partners
records.status_note: Running 2021-2027; Regulation (EU) 2025/2005 (adopted 16 December 2025, OJ 23 December 2025) set the EU compartment guarantee at about €29.05bn (+€2.9bn), and a June 2026 Commission-EIB agreement added €22bn of strategic financing expected to mobilise about €70bn by end of the current MFF.

records.name: Horizon Europe – the Framework Programme for Research and Innovation
records.description: Horizon Europe is the EU's research and innovation framework programme for 2021-2027, established by Regulation (EU) 2021/695, with indicative funding of €93.5 billion after the MFF mid-term review. It is structured in three pillars (Excellent Science; Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness with six clusters; Innovative Europe including the EIC) plus a widening/ERA part. The main 2026-2027 work programme (€14 billion) was adopted on 11 December 2025, and a successor programme for 2028-2034 with a proposed €175 billion budget is under negotiation.
objectives: Strengthen the EU's scientific and technological base and the European Research Area
Tackle global challenges and boost industrial competitiveness through collaborative research
Support breakthrough innovation and scale-up via the European Innovation Council
Widen participation across Member States
records.institution: European Commission (DG RTD) and executive agencies (ERCEA, REA, EISMEA, HaDEA, CINEA)
records.status_note: Runs 2021-2027 with 22 associated non-EU countries; the final 2026-2027 work programme is being implemented, and the Commission's 16 July 2025 proposal for the 2028-2034 successor (€175bn, linked to the European Competitiveness Fund) awaits agreement.

records.name: European Chips Act
records.description: Regulation (EU) 2023/1781 establishes a framework to strengthen Europe's semiconductor ecosystem, aiming to double the EU's global market share to 20% by 2030. It created the Chips for Europe Initiative (pilot lines, design capacities, competence centres and a Chips Fund for start-ups and scale-ups via the EIC and InvestEU), a framework for first-of-a-kind facilities and a supply-crisis coordination mechanism. On 3 June 2026 the Commission proposed a Chips Act 2.0 that would repeal and replace it.
objectives: Double the EU's share of global semiconductor production to 20% by 2030
Build design, pilot-line and testing capacity through the Chips for Europe Initiative
Attract investment in first-of-a-kind manufacturing facilities
Monitor supply chains and respond to semiconductor shortages
Finance semiconductor start-ups and scale-ups through the Chips Fund
records.institution: European Commission (DG CNECT); Chips Joint Undertaking; European Semiconductor Board
records.status_note: Regulation (EU) 2023/1781 has applied since 21 September 2023; the Chips Act 2.0 proposal COM(2026) 504 (procedure 2026/0139(COD)) of 3 June 2026, which would repeal it and launch a Chips for Europe Initiative 2.0, is pending before Parliament and Council.

records.name: Scaleup Europe Fund
records.description: The Scaleup Europe Fund is a market-based growth fund within the EIC Fund umbrella, targeting about €5 billion, with the European Commission committing €1 billion as a founding investor on equal terms with private investors. Managed by EQT, it makes growth and scale-up investments of €100 million and above in strategic technologies such as AI, quantum, semiconductors, robotics, energy, space, biotech and medtech. It was launched at the EIC Summit on 3 June 2026; the strategy's companion 'European Innovation Investment Pact' was launched on 22 September 2026 under the name European Institutional Investors Pact.
objectives: Close the late-stage financing gap for European deep tech scaleups
Crowd in private institutional capital alongside a €1bn EU commitment
Keep strategic-technology scaleups headquartered in Europe
Channel institutional investors' capital into EU venture and growth funds (via the companion Institutional Investors Pact)
records.institution: European Commission / European Innovation Council (EIC Fund); fund manager EQT; EIB Group (Institutional Investors Pact)
records.geography: EU27 + Horizon Europe associated countries (Pillar III)
records.status_note: No initiative named 'European Innovation Investment Pact' exists as a launched instrument: it was the working name in the May 2025 strategy and was launched on 22 September 2026 as the European Institutional Investors Pact (EIIP); this record covers the Scaleup Europe Fund, launched 3 June 2026 with first investments expected in autumn 2026.

records.name: Artificial Intelligence Act
records.description: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 sets harmonised, risk-based rules for placing AI systems and general-purpose AI models on the EU market, banning certain practices and imposing obligations on high-risk systems. It was amended in 2026 by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), which postponed high-risk obligations, added new prohibitions and extended SME simplifications to small mid-caps.
objectives: Ensure AI systems placed on the EU market are safe and respect fundamental rights
Prohibit unacceptable-risk AI practices
Set requirements for high-risk AI systems and general-purpose AI models
Support innovation through regulatory sandboxes and simplified rules for SMEs and small mid-caps
records.status_note: Prohibitions and AI literacy apply since 2 Feb 2025, GPAI obligations since 2 Aug 2025 and the Act generally since 2 Aug 2026; after the AI Omnibus, Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2 Dec 2027 and Annex I (product-embedded) high-risk obligations from 2 Aug 2028.

records.name: Data Act
records.description: Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 sets harmonised rules on fair access to and use of data generated by connected products and related services, including B2B and B2G data sharing, unfair contractual terms and switching between data processing (cloud) services. It applies since 12 September 2025; amendments are pending under the Commission's Digital Omnibus proposal of 19 November 2025.
objectives: Give users of connected products access to the data they generate and the right to share it with third parties
Protect businesses, especially SMEs, against unfair data-sharing contract terms
Make it easier to switch between cloud and data processing providers, removing switching charges
Enable public-sector access to private data in exceptional situations
records.status_note: Applies since 12 Sep 2025; the Article 3(1) data-access-by-design obligation applies to connected products placed on the market after 12 Sep 2026, switching charges are to be fully removed from 12 Jan 2027, and Chapter IV extends to certain pre-existing contracts from 12 Sep 2027.

records.name: Digital Markets Act
records.description: Regulation (EU) 2022/1925 imposes ex-ante obligations and prohibitions on large online platforms designated as gatekeepers to keep digital markets contestable and fair. Seven gatekeepers are designated (Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta, Microsoft, Booking), and the Commission has adopted non-compliance decisions with fines, including €890 million against Google in July 2026.
objectives: Ensure contestable and fair digital markets where gatekeepers operate
Prohibit self-preferencing and unfair practices by gatekeepers
Open opportunities for business users, developers and alternative services (interoperability, data portability, steering)
records.institution: European Commission (DG COMP and DG CNECT)
records.status_note: Applicable since 2 May 2023; designated gatekeepers must comply within six months of designation, and enforcement through non-compliance decisions is ongoing.

records.name: Digital Services Act
records.description: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 sets rules for online intermediaries and platforms on illegal content, transparency, and systemic risk management, with the strictest obligations for very large online platforms and search engines supervised by the Commission. It has applied to all online intermediaries since 17 February 2024, and the Commission has issued fines against X, Temu and AliExpress.

Increase transparency and accountability of online platforms, including recommender systems and advertising
Require very large platforms and search engines to assess and mitigate systemic risks

records.name: Cyber Resilience Act
records.description: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 introduces horizontal cybersecurity requirements for hardware and software products with digital elements placed on the EU market, covering their design, development and vulnerability handling across the life cycle. Manufacturers' obligations to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents through ENISA's Single Reporting Platform apply since 11 September 2026, with main obligations applying from 11 December 2027.
objectives: Ensure hardware and software products with digital elements are placed on the market with fewer vulnerabilities
Make manufacturers responsible for cybersecurity throughout the product life cycle
Require reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents
Help users take cybersecurity into account when choosing and using products
records.status_note: Chapter IV (conformity assessment bodies) applies since 11 Jun 2026 and Article 14 reporting obligations since 11 Sep 2026; the Regulation applies in full from 11 Dec 2027.

records.name: Clean Industrial Deal
records.description: The Clean Industrial Deal (COM(2025) 85) is the Commission's joint roadmap for competitiveness and decarbonisation, aiming to lower energy costs, support energy-intensive industries and clean-tech manufacturing, and create lead markets for EU-made clean products. It plans to mobilise over €100 billion and proposed an Industrial Decarbonisation Bank targeting €100 billion; follow-ups include the Industrial Accelerator Act (March 2026) and Innovation Fund heat auctions run as Bank pilots.
objectives: Make decarbonisation a driver of industrial competitiveness
Lower energy costs for industry and accelerate electrification
Create lead markets for EU-made clean and low-carbon products
Support energy-intensive industries and clean-tech manufacturing
Increase circularity (circular material use rate from 11.8% to 24% by 2030)
records.status_note: Being rolled out through follow-up acts and funding: the Industrial Accelerator Act was proposed on 4 Mar 2026 and awaits adoption, and the €100bn Industrial Decarbonisation Bank is being piloted through Innovation Fund heat auctions.

records.name: European Green Deal
records.description: The European Green Deal (COM(2019) 640) is the Commission's growth strategy to make the EU climate-neutral by 2050, with a legally binding framework set by the European Climate Law. It is implemented through sectoral legislation; in 2026 the Climate Law was amended to set a 90% net emissions reduction target for 2040.
objectives: Make the EU climate-neutral by 2050 (legally binding under the European Climate Law)
Cut net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 compared with 1990
Reach a 90% net emissions reduction by 2040 (85% domestic, up to 5% international credits)
Decouple economic growth from resource use
records.status_note: A strategy being implemented through legislation: the European Climate Law makes 2050 neutrality binding, and its amendment setting the 2040 90% target (Regulation (EU) 2026/667) has been in force since 7 Apr 2026.

records.name: Digital Europe Programme
records.description: The Digital Europe Programme, established by Regulation (EU) 2021/694, funds the deployment of digital technologies and capacities across the EU in 2021-2027, complementing research funding under Horizon Europe. Its specific objectives cover high-performance computing, AI, cybersecurity and trust, advanced digital skills, deployment and interoperability, and semiconductors.
objectives: High-performance computing
Artificial intelligence
Cybersecurity and trust
Advanced digital skills
Deployment and best use of digital capacities and interoperability
Semiconductors (added in 2023)
records.geography: EU27 + Digital Europe associated countries (EEA EFTA, Ukraine, Western Balkans, Türkiye, Moldova)
records.status_note: Runs from 1 Jan 2021 to 31 Dec 2027 and is implemented through the 2025-2027 work programme, amended in October 2025 and March 2026.
